title: Grill first, then go AFK: Gemini 4 Neon, legal markups, Cameranu
summary: Google's Gemini 4 Neon muddles model choice further, a new legal-services paper shows why cheaper expertise can raise premium prices, and a Dutch retailer's failed chatbot became a set of narrow agents that work. The deep dive follows Matt Pocock's 21,000-line run to show how pinning down decisions before an agent starts lets it work unattended.
shownotes:
Gemini 4 Neon: mid-tier model at $3/$15 per million tokens, 32% cheaper per task than Carbon per Google, but currently the priciest per token until Carbon's price doubles on 1 December; route on cost per solved task.
AI and legal services (Zhang, Esposito, Yang): self-representation up 5.7 to 6.55 percentage points in FY2025; top firms raise rates as price-sensitive work leaves.
Cameranu's Flits: a failed chatbot rebuilt as single-task agents now handles 25% of customer contacts.
Anthropic IPO priced at $83 (ticker ANT): what the S-1 commentary says about compute split, margins and model churn, plus Tyler Cowen's debt-versus-equity reading.
Deep dive: Matt Pocock's skills workflow - grill, prototype, spec, tracer-bullet tickets, parallel fresh-context subagents, two-axis review, and turning review comments into rules. Install: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official, then /setup-matt-pocock-skills per repo.
